title: Don’t waste what God did for you.
paragraphs: Don’t waste what God did for you.
That’s the thunder inside 2 Corinthians 6:1.
Paul says, “We then, as workers together with him, beseech you also that ye receive not the grace of God in vain.”
Read that slowly.

Grace can be offered...
and still ignored.

Mercy can reach your house...
and still leave your habits untouched.

You can cry in church, raise your hands, post the verse, say “God is good”—
and still waste the very grace that came to rescue you.
That is sobering.

Because grace was never given to make sin comfortable.
Grace came to break chains.
Grace came to pull you out.
Grace came to make dead hearts live again through Jesus Christ.
But here’s what we miss:

Paul is not saying grace is weak.
He is saying our hearts can treat holy things casually.

We can be forgiven,
but refuse to repent.

Invited,
but never surrender.

Loved by God,
but still flirt with the same darkness Christ died to free us from.

Beloved, don’t waste the cross.
Don’t waste the blood.
Don’t waste the prayers God answered just to bring you back to Himself.

Jesus did not save you so you could stay half-awake, half-committed, half-clean.
He saved you to make you new.

So if God has been calling you, convicting you, correcting you—
that is not rejection.
That is mercy knocking.
Answer it.

Turn fully.
Repent deeply.
Walk clean.
Live grateful.
And let the grace of God produce a life that proves Christ is real.

There is still hope for you.
Even now.

The same grace you may have neglected is the same grace that can restore you—
if you come back to Jesus with your whole heart.

Don’t waste what God did.
Let grace have its full work.
“Don’t receive the grace of God in vain.” — 2 Corinthians 6:1
